PART 1 · LEARN

1. What is the idea of this lab?

Imagine a temperature sensor in your classroom. You want to see its readings on your smartphone without connecting a cable. Bluetooth allows nearby devices to exchange data wirelessly, just like a phone sends sound to wireless headphones.

Important: This webpage simulates the data journey inside your browser. It does not establish a real Bluetooth connection.
PART 2 · UNDERSTAND

2. Arduino Uno or ESP32?

Example: The sensor measures 28°C. The ESP32 prepares the message Temperature: 28 C. Bluetooth transfers the message to a compatible phone app.

PART 4 · CODE EXAMPLES

4. Serial communication vs. Bluetooth

A. Wokwi Serial Monitor

Open Wokwi, create an ESP32 project and paste this sketch. It prints a sample value, not a real sensor reading.

int temperature = 25;

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
}

void loop() {
  Serial.print("Temperature: ");
  Serial.print(temperature);
  Serial.println(" C");
  delay(2000);
}
Expected Serial Monitor output
Temperature: 25 C
Temperature: 25 C
Temperature: 25 C

B. Real Bluetooth (optional reference)

For a compatible physical original ESP32 and Bluetooth Classic serial app (typically Android).

#include "BluetoothSerial.h"

BluetoothSerial BT;
int temperature = 25;

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  BT.begin("Smart_Classroom");
}

void loop() {
  BT.print("Temperature: ");
  BT.print(temperature);
  BT.println(" C");
  delay(2000);
}

Pair/connect using a compatible Bluetooth serial app and receive the sample message. This example is not a required Wokwi task.

Serial communicationBluetooth communication

int temperature = 25

Creates a sample temperature value.

Serial.begin(115200)

Starts serial communication at 115200 baud.

Serial.print() / BT.print()

Writes the message to the chosen interface.

delay(2000)

Waits two seconds before repeating.
